purpose: Does working only with the schema actually work? Execute an approved recipe and compare to a frozen expected table. Plan v1 sec.10 step 6, deferred four times.
framed_question: Another question to answer is if only working with schema really works -- that's what we are relying on in the end.

claims.A: Can an AGENT define the frame from structure alone? UNTESTED; separate freeze; depends on B.
claims.B: Is a RECIPE sufficient to do the job? NEVER TESTED -- this experiment.

L1.description: the workbook the recipe was written for

L2.description: next month's file: six products, the total row moved. THE PAYOFF CLAIM -- define once, run on next month's file, no model in the loop.
must_be_absent: the YHTEENSA row, wherever it moved to

G1.gap: The format has no way to say HOW a date is written -- no format string, no locale. The executor cannot honour the declaration without guessing dd.mm.yyyy, and guessing is what this programme does not do.
G1.expected: the value stays the raw string '3.2.2026' AND declared_types_honoured is False for this field
G1.why_it_matters: G1 is the first concrete answer to the question. Working only with the schema DOES work -- up to the point where the schema cannot say something the job needs. Counting those points is the measurement.

grading.L1_pass: executor output == frozen expected_rows exactly, order included
grading.gaps: declared_types_honoured recorded per field; G1 predicted False

decision_table.condition: L1 and L2 both match and gaps == ['G1']
decision_table.outcome: PASS_AS_PREDICTED -- a recipe does the job, and one named thing the schema cannot say
FAIL -- record the diff; do NOT adjust the expected table
RESULT_MORE_GAPS -- record each; this is the measurement, not a failure

decision_table.condition: the executor needs information the recipe does not carry
decision_table.outcome: FAIL_INSUFFICIENT -- the honest negative answer, and the most important possible result

hard_stop: Execution only. No LLM, including for parsing a date.
No changes to the frozen grammar, to recipe format v1.1/v1.2/v1.3, to any recorded K result, or to any frozen fixture.
If the executor needs something the format lacks, that is a GAP -- never patched into the format mid-run. Patching would convert the measurement into a tautology.
stated_limitations: One recipe, two workbooks. This establishes that a recipe CAN execute correctly, not that the format covers the space of real provider files.
The expected tables were written by hand from the fixtures, so they test the executor, not the fixtures.
Expressiveness across many shapes is a separate measurement (an L2-style breadth arm), not attempted here.
Deterministic and fully repeatable: no LLM, no seeds, no sampling.
